model.display_name: Confucius4-R2T2 (streaming speech-to-text: Qwen3-ASR-1.7B fine-tune, one clip of up to 30 s per message)
model.architecture: Qwen3-ASR: in-graph Whisper-style log-mel (128 bins, the original feature extractor's STFT / Slaney filterbank / normalization) -> 24-layer audio encoder (104-token attention windows) -> projector -> 28-layer Qwen3 LM; LiteRT-LM generic audio path (raw 16 kHz PCM in 160-sample frames, no mel extraction in the runtime)
model.license: netease-model-use-license-agreement (MODEL_LICENSE / MODEL_LICENSE_zh in the repo; the Chinese text prevails)

session_defaults.notes: Greedy decoding (top_k 1, top_p 1, temperature 0) for every measurement. One conversation per clip of up to 30 s; the answer is 'language <name><asr_text><transcript>', split it at <asr_text>.

variants.quantization: LM: int8 dynamic weights with an int8 embedding table; audio encoder: fp16 weights, fp32 compute, in-graph log-mel, 30 s window (3000 frames x 160 samples at 16 kHz -> 390 audio tokens)

recommended.reason: 155 clips end to end (litert-lm-api 0.17.1, one conversation per clip): RTF 0.053 with the LM on the GPU (WebGPU over Metal, prefill_128 and decode fully delegated) vs 0.124 on the CPU; FLEURS en WER 4.52 % / zh CER 6.45 % / ja CER 6.06 % vs 4.43 / 6.40 / 6.21 on the CPU; the audio encoder stays on CPU (audio_backend cpu)

Galaxy S26: the LM on OpenCL (prefill_128 and decode fully delegated) transcribed 5/5 example clips with a peak private footprint of 1,932 MB vs 7,470 MB for the CPU leg (run without a weight cache); per-process wall 5.6-9.3 s vs 10.4-19.6 s, both under a CPU frequency cap - verified choice, not a measured speed win

platform_notes: One message = one clip of up to 30 s: the runtime zero-fills the 30 s window after the clip and the encoder emits 390 audio tokens per window (encoding and prefill cost the same for any clip length). Clips longer than 30 s were not tested

The answer is 'language <name><asr_text><transcript>'. To force the language, send the text item 'language Chinese<asr_text>' (or another language name) in the same message as the audio: the template puts the user's text items after 'assistant\n', where the original code puts a forced language

Template = the litert-torch Qwen3-ASR prompt (<|im_start|>user<|audio_start|>…<|audio_end|><|im_end|><|im_start|>assistant\n, no system turn); system messages are ignored. The original repository's prompt (empty system turn) scored FLEURS zh CER 10.75 % / ja CER 9.33 % with this file (language tags English/None on Mandarin clips, Chinese numerals, one Mandarin and one Japanese clip translated into English)
audio_backend must be cpu (audio_backend=CPU() / --audio_backend=cpu); the LM runs on cpu or gpu

Accuracy, FLEURS test 50 clips per language, greedy: macOS CPU en WER 4.43 % / zh CER 6.40 % / ja CER 6.21 %, macOS LM-on-GPU 4.52 % / 6.45 % / 6.06 % (original model in PyTorch fp32 with the same prompt 4.43 % / 6.24 % / 6.21 %); no empty transcript

The first load writes about 3.0 GB of CPU weight caches (encoder 1.27 GB, LM 1.73 GB) into cache_dir, or next to the model file when none is set; that first load peaked at 6.6 GB RSS on macOS (4.5 GB with the caches present)

Streaming: the original r2t2 streaming_transcribe loop (2 s chunks; the accumulated audio plus the previous answer minus its last 5 tokens as a text item, in a new conversation per call) runs through these calls; about 1 s per call on Apple M4 Max CPU (211 calls over 35 clips; FLEURS scores of the 30 FLEURS clips equal the offline scores)

Galaxy S26 rows are reference values: the CPU frequency limit fell from 3.63 / 4.74 GHz to 1.79 / 1.75 GHz during the CPU leg and the GPU leg started under it; the CPU leg ran without a weight cache (cache_dir did not exist), peak private 7,470 MB; LM on OpenCL 1,932 MB; transcripts equal to the macOS CPU run on 15 of 20 (CPU) and 4 of 5 (GPU) clips

measured.source: 155-clip transcription (FLEURS test en_us / cmn_hans_cn / ja_jp x 50 + 5 example clips, 1,836.1 s of audio), one conversation per clip, greedy, LM and audio encoder on CPU (4 threads): 227.1 s processing, RTF 0.124, per clip 1.08-2.64 s (median 1.42 s); peak_memory_mb = /usr/bin/time maximum resident set size of a second 155-clip run with the weight caches present (4,546,035,712 B / 2^20; transcripts identical 155/155)

same 155 clips, LM on the GPU (WebGPU over Metal; 'Replacing 1298 out of 1298 node(s) with delegate (LITERT_WEBGPU)' for prefill_128 and 1244 of 1244 for decode), audio encoder on CPU (4 threads): 96.9 s processing, RTF 0.053, per clip 0.49-1.06 s (median 0.61 s); peak_memory_mb = /usr/bin/time maximum resident set size (2,682,519,552 B / 2^20)

20 shortest clips of the set (127.6 s of audio), one process per clip, --num_cpu_threads=4 --audio_backend=cpu, no weight cache (cache_dir missing); wall per process including engine load 10.4-19.6 s; 'Peak private footprint' from --report_peak_memory_footprint on the first clip; scaling_max_freq fell to 1785600 / 1747200 kHz during the leg (reference value under a thermal cap); transcripts = macOS CPU 15/20

5 example clips, one process per clip, LM on OpenCL ('Replacing 1298 out of 1298 node(s) with delegate (LITERT_CL)' for prefill_128, 1244 of 1244 for decode), audio encoder on CPU; wall per process including engine load 5.6-9.3 s; started under the CPU frequency cap left by the CPU leg (reference value); transcripts = macOS CPU 4/5

known_issues: The audio encoder does not run on the GPU delegate: with audio_backend=GPU() create_conversation fails ('BATCH_MATMUL: Not supported batched mat mul case: non-constant tensor' on macOS WebGPU); keep audio_backend=cpu
The original streaming procedure's committed text (latest answer minus its last 5 tokens) shrinks by 1-2 characters when a call adds fewer than 5 tokens (2 of 211 calls with this file's prompt)
